disease_label_per_paper: Recurrent sickle cell disease acute chest syndrome treated with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
presentation_summary: Young adult with homozygous SS sickle cell disease, chronic pulmonary hypertension, and prior severe ACS.
Second severe episode occurred after vaso-occlusive crisis with pain, dyspnea, and inflammatory syndrome.
At ICU admission she had fever, dyspnea, hypercapnic acute respiratory failure, bilateral alveolar condensation, cardiomegaly, and moderate pleural effusion.
Blood gas showed pH 7.28, PaCO2 55 mmHg, and PaO2/FiO2 140.
Echocardiography showed acute cor pulmonale physiology with severe pulmonary hypertension; labs showed acute renal dysfunction.

risk_context.source_text_value: Medical history included homozygous SS sickle cell disease.

Respiratory failure occurred after vaso-occlusive crisis.

observations.source_text_value: Hypercapnic acute respiratory failure was present.
Required noninvasive ventilation alternating with high-flow oxygen before ECMO-level deterioration.
X-ray and CT showed major bilateral alveolar condensation.
Echocardiography showed acute cor pulmonale with systolic pulmonary artery pressure above 60 mmHg.
Creatinine was 18.3 mg/L, converted to 1.83 mg/dL.
Urea was 0.97 g/L; BUN equivalent is approximately 45.3 mg/dL.
The paper describes acute biological renal failure.
